transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-29
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Jimenez (Redwood SE), Laura Chen (CISO - Mountain Trust), Rajiv Kapoor (Head of Platform), Marta Silva (Legal), Tom Erickson (DevOps)

Summary: Short discovery to surface Mountain Trust's data residency, regulatory (GDPR/HIPAA/financial) and logging constraints and to align on Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private options. Customer strongly prefers bank-resident data; needs KMS/HSM support, audit log controls, configurable retention, and clear encryption in transit/at rest statements.

Topics: data residency, SOC2/HIPAA scope, private deployment (VPC/on-prem), KMS/HSM, audit logs, SSO/SAML, RBAC, data retention & redaction, egress patterns, pilot next steps.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Sofia, AE at Redwood, and with me is Carlos, our solutions engineer. How's everyone?
[00:07] Laura: Thanks, Sofia. Hi, I'm Laura, CISO for Mountain Trust. We carved out 45 mins for this. Quick context: we're evaluating providers for an internal assistant and document indexing project, primary concern is data residency and regulatory controls.
[00:18] Sofia: Great, that's exactly what we wanted to understand. Rajiv, do you want to give a quick overview of current infra?
[00:24] Rajiv: Sure. We're multi-cloud, primary workloads in AWS us-east-1 and a couple of on-prem clusters for sensitive workloads. We have strict rules for PII and FIs. Anything classified as financial records must stay in our bank-owned VPC or on prem.
[00:36] Tom: And from Ops side, we don't want logs that contain raw customer PII leaving the network.
[00:41] Carlos: Understood. For clarity, are you mostly interested in Hosted API, Dedicated, or Private? Or want options?
[00:49] Laura: Options. We had an initial review of hosted but our security team flagged it because of logging and data residency. We need to know what Redwood can guarantee for data not leaving the EU/US regions and how logs are handled.
[01:02] Sofia: Got it. High-level: our Hosted API is multi-region with contractual commitments and regional controls, but for strict bank-only data residency and managed keys customers typically pick Dedicated or Private. Dedicated gives you reserved capacity in a customer-only pool with isolation; Private gives you customer-controlled deployment in your VPC or on-prem.
[01:21] Marta: On legal side, we need to know about subprocessors, data processing addenda, and HIPAA BAAs. Does Redwood sign BAAs?
[01:29] Sofia: We do offer BAAs for customers that need HIPAA coverage; we'll include the BAA template and our subprocessors list in the compliance pack.
[01:36] Laura: For GDPR, we need data residency within EU for EU customer data. Can Redwood pin requests and storage to eu-west-1 only?
[01:44] Carlos: Yes - for Dedicated and Private we can ensure routing to specific regions and even specific clusters. For Hosted, there are regional endpoints and we can provide contractual commitments, but some internal logs for platform health may be global unless you choose a Dedicated or Private controlling log export.
[02:01] Rajiv: What about encryption keys? We need to integrate with our AWS KMS / HSM, and ideally customer-managed keys so Redwood can't decrypt tokens at rest.
[02:11] Carlos: Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM - your keys stay in your account and Redwood's control plane doesn't have access. Dedicated supports CMK integrations as well, but the exact flow depends on whether it's Redwood-managed infra in your VPC or fully customer-hosted. For Hosted, we use Redwood-managed keys but can support envelope encryption workflows for certain contracts.
[02:31] Tom: Can we ensure request-level redaction in transit? Like prevent full utterances from being stored in logs at any step?
[02:38] Sofia: We have configurable logging levels. With Dedicated and Private, you can disable request-body logging and only retain structured metrics. We also provide automatic PII masking options at the SDK/agent level.
[02:50] Laura: Audit logs are critical - who accessed what model, when, and the exact requester. Can we export logs to our SIEM and also keep immutable audit trails?
[02:59] Carlos: Yes. Both Dedicated and Private support outbound log export to syslog/S3/Kafka and we can produce structured audit events. We also support write-once logs if you want immutability, typically via your own S3 lifecycle or WORM storage.
[03:12] Marta: Any certifications? SOC2, ISO, PCI?
[03:16] Sofia: We're SOC 2 Type II and working toward ISO; PCI depends on the scope and whether you tokenize. We'll include our latest reports in the pack.
[03:26] Rajiv: Performance question - if we go Private in our VPC, what's the expected latency difference versus Hosted? We need sub-100ms token latency for some use cases.
[03:35] Carlos: Latency will depend on your infra. If you deploy Private in your us-east-1 region close to your app tier and use our optimized runtime, you can meet low-latency SLOs. Dedicated pools are tuned for throughput; they can also meet low latency, but you should expect slight increases due to routing if the Dedicated cluster is in a different AZ. We'll run benchmarks during a pilot.
[03:55] Tom: About data retention - do you keep prompt/response data by default? How configurable is retention?
[04:01] Sofia: By default Hosted keeps logs and transcripts for 30 days for debugging, but we have retention controls and can disable storing prompts/responses. Dedicated and Private give fine-grained retention policies down to per-route retention.
[04:14] Laura: We also need the ability to purge data on demand for legal holds and support e-discovery.
[04:19] Carlos: We support on-demand purge APIs and can coordinate full dataset deletes in Private deployments. For Hosted, we have a purge process and audit trail; turnaround times differ and we'll document SLAs.
[04:31] Marta: On subprocessors - if you use a managed Hosted service, where do backups live? Any cross-border replication?
[04:37] Sofia: Backups for Hosted are region-scoped but we do have failover regions; cross-region replication is configurable and typically disabled for regulated customers. We'll include the subprocessors list and backup patterns in the compliance packet.
[04:50] Rajiv: Is there an option to run model weights entirely on-prem, or do you always connect to Redwood control plane?
[04:57] Carlos: For Private on-prem, you can host model weights entirely in your environment. Our control plane can be configured as a customer-managed control plane or a lightweight agent that talks only to your endpoint. We can offer an air-gapped deployment for high-security customers.
[05:11] Tom: For billing and telemetry, what minimal telemetry is required to run the runtime? We can't have customer PII in metrics sent to Redwood.
[05:19] Carlos: Telemetry is configurable. The minimal heartbeat includes anonymized resource metrics; you can opt out of request-level telemetry. For Dedicated/Private we can keep telemetry inside your VPC and only send aggregated billing metrics.
[05:31] Laura: Regarding HIPAA and BAAs - do you have experience with other banks or healthcare orgs?
[05:36] Sofia: Yes, we've signed BAAs and worked with healthcare customers. We'll include references and case studies where possible.
[05:43] Rajiv: On the subject of model behavior - we need guardrails for PII not to be returned in responses. Do you support deterministic redaction or filters?
[05:52] Carlos: We provide pre- and post-processing hooks for redaction, plus model-level safety filters. For high-assurance use cases you can process classified texts in a Private deployment and run a redaction pass before storage.
[06:05] Marta: Legal wants clarity on liability - if PHI or financial data leaks via model output, how is liability apportioned?
[06:12] Sofia: That's part legal negotiation; generally liability and indemnities depend on contract and deployment mode. For Private on-prem with customer keys, liability shifts more to the customer, but we'll provide indemnity language per standard templates; we'll hand this to legal for review.
[06:26] Laura: We need to map this to our internal classification. We'll share a doc.
[06:30] Tom: Network and egress: if the model calls out to external tools or retrieval augmentations, can we block egress entirely?
[06:38] Carlos: Yes. In Private deployments you control egress via security groups and our agent doesn't allow external callbacks unless you enable plugin/tool-calls. In Dedicated you can apply policies to disable tool/plugin calls.
[06:51] Rajiv: How do we handle keys for embeddings and caching? We don't want cached KV stores to contain raw PII in Redwood-managed storage.
[07:00] Carlos: For Dedicated and Private, cache can be colocated in your environment or encrypted with customer keys. For Hosted, we advise tokenization or PII-stripping before embedding.
[07:11] Sofia: Quick note - customers sometimes do prefix-caching in their app tier and keep sensitive data out of the model inputs.
[07:17] Marta: Can you produce a list of all endpoints and what logs are produced per endpoint? Legal needs that.
[07:23] Sofia: Yes, we'll include an endpoint and logging matrix in the pack - absolute detail on what each endpoint logs and how to disable it.
[07:31] Laura: For GDPR DSARs, we need an exportability guarantee of data tied to a user. Can we extract full request/response history on-demand?
[07:41] Carlos: Yes, for Dedicated and Private you control storage and can run exports. For Hosted we provide DSAR support via our compliance team; export will be subject to audit and may take longer but we have processes.
[07:55] Rajiv: Any reference architecture for a hybrid setup where some traffic goes to Hosted (non-sensitive) and sensitive traffic stays in Private?
[08:03] Carlos: Absolutely; we often recommend smart routing by policy - route by workload type, sensitivity tags, or headers. Redwood supports policy-based routing and automatic fallback. We'll attach sample configs.
[08:16] Tom: How about SSO and RBAC? We need SAML/SCIM integration and per-route permissions.
[08:23] Sofia: We support SAML SSO, SCIM for provisioning, and RBAC with role-based access to routes and models. In Private you can integrate with your IAM and enforce network-level controls.
[08:36] Marta: Is there an option for immutable audit logs for compliance teams?
[08:41] Carlos: Yes, we can stream logs to your WORM storage or S3 with object lock for immutability.
[08:49] Laura: What's the typical timeline for a Private deployment?
[08:53] Sofia: For a VPC-hosted Private deployment on cloud, typical timeline is 4-8 weeks including infra provisioning, keys, and security review. On-prem or air-gapped can take longer depending on approvals. Dedicated is faster - often 2-4 weeks.
[09:05] Rajiv: For the pilot, we'd like a small Dedicated pool in our account or a Private VPC deploy to test with redaction and purge flows.
[09:13] Sofia: Sounds good. We can propose a pilot SOW. For the pilot we'll include benchmarks (latency/cost), a security deep-dive, and operational runbook.
[09:21] Tom: A couple more specifics - do you support customer-hosted model registries and pinned model versions? We need to freeze model versions for audits.
[09:29] Carlos: Yes. You can pin model versions and we support external model registries in Private. Dedicated also supports pinning and rollout policies.
[09:37] Marta: Contractual data residency - can you add a clause that guarantees no cross-border replication for certain datasets?
[09:44] Sofia: We can add contractual data residency clauses for Dedicated/Private customers; for Hosted we'll limit replication by region but it depends on failover SLAs.
[09:53] Laura: Let's talk about evidence - we'll need an initial SOC2 report, BAA, subprocessors list, and network diagrams.
[09:59] Sofia: We'll compile those. Carlos, can you own network diagram?
[10:03] Carlos: Yep, I'll draft a network diagram for Private and Dedicated flows.
[10:07] Rajiv: If we want envelope encryption with our CMKs, how does key rotation work?
[10:12] Carlos: We support key rotation via your KMS; we'll re-encrypt caches and storage using new envelopes, and you control rotation policies. For Hosted scenarios, we have rotation support but keys are managed by Redwood; rotation is coordinated with customers.
[10:25] Marta: Any legal blockers you anticipate?
[10:29] Sofia: None immediate; it will be standard negotiation around indemnities, data processing terms, and KMS responsibilities. We'll surface typical redlines we see.
[10:38] Tom: For observability, can we get token-level cost and latency breakdowns without exposing content?
[10:44] Carlos: Yes, we provide token-level metrics and latency traces while redacting content. You can export metrics to your monitoring stack.
[10:52] Laura: Great. On the team side, who will run the security deep-dive?
[10:56] Sofia: Carlos and a Security Solutions Architect will join; we'll also include our compliance engineer.
[11:03] Rajiv: Let's close - action items?
[11:06] Sofia: Recap: I'll send compliance pack (SOC2, HIPAA/BAA, subprocessors, endpoint logging matrix); Carlos will prepare network diagrams and sample routing policy + pilot SOW; Mountain Trust will share data classification and retention policy. We'll schedule the security deep-dive the week of Apr 5.
[11:22] Marta: Sounds good. One last thing - pricing ballpark for Dedicated vs Private so procurement knows what to expect?
[11:29] Sofia: We'll include ballpark pricing and a pilot SOW in the follow-up.
[11:33] Laura: Thanks everyone.
[11:35] Sofia: Thanks all. We'll follow up by end of week with docs and proposed times.

End of transcript.
